findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error, breaking the main embed view
findings.body: The header block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. The ERB compiler emits the literal Ruby `end if`, which closes the `if`/`else` and then starts a *new*, never-closed `if` statement (Ruby allows a newline between `if` and its condition, so the following buffer append becomes the condition). The template therefore raises a SyntaxError (`unexpected end-of-input`) whenever it is compiled, so `GET /embed/best` will 500 for every topic that already has an embed. It should simply be `<%- end %>`. Note the specs never render this template with posts present (TopicView is mocked), so the failure is not caught by tests.

findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string literal with no escaping. Only the *host* part of the referer is validated in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable; the path and query are arbitrary, so a URL on the embeddable host such as `http://host/page?x='+alert(document.cookie)+'` (or one containing `</script>`) breaks out of the string and executes attacker-controlled script in the context of the Discourse origin, with the visitor's session. Escape it, e.g. `<%= j request.referer %>` / `json_escape`, and preferably send only the origin (scheme://host:port) rather than the full URL.

findings.title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized remote HTML as `cooked` (stored XSS)
findings.body: `cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`, bypassing PrettyText/sanitization entirely. TopicEmbed.import creates posts with this cook method from content fetched from a third party (Jobs::PollFeed passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` straight through with no tag/attribute filtering), and the embed view and normal topic view render `cooked` with `raw`. A hostile or compromised feed can therefore inject `<script>`, `onerror=`, iframes, etc. into forum pages for all users. The HTML needs to be run through a sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize with a whitelist, as ruby-readability does for the import_remote path) before being stored as cooked.

findings.title: `i.content.scrub` breaks for RSS feeds and on Ruby < 2.1
findings.body: The job claims to support "RSS or ATOM", but SimpleRSS only exposes `content` for Atom `<content>` / `content:encoded`; a plain RSS 2.0 item only has `description`. For such feeds `i.content` is nil and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, and because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` the import silently never happens. Additionally `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby >= 2.1, so on Ruby 2.0 (still supported per the Gemfile/platform notes) even Atom feeds raise NoMethodError. Fall back to `i.description`/`content_encoded` and guard the encoding scrub.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching and can be bypassed
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a *substring* of the configured Discourse URL rather than comparing the actual origin. For example with `discourseUrl = 'http://evil.com.discourse.example.com/'` the origin `http://evil.com` passes the test, letting a third-party frame drive the resize handler. Compare against a precomputed origin with strict equality instead (and note the message payload is otherwise trusted).

findings.title: Update path crashes when the embedded post no longer exists
findings.body: In the `else` branch, `post = embed.post` is passed straight to `PostRevisor.new(post)`. If the original post (or its topic) was deleted/trashed, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor#revise!` immediately raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw`, so the poll_feed job (retry: false) or the embed retrieval job dies for that URL and the embed stays permanently broken. Guard for a missing post and either recreate the topic or skip the row.

findings.title: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string argument
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n<small>..."` appends in place to the string the caller passed in. Any caller that reuses or caches that string (or passes a frozen/literal string, which raises RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String) is affected, and the mutation is invisible from the call site. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

findings.title: Adding `force: true` to an already-shipped migration can drop a populated table
findings.body: This migration already exists in the repository history, so installs have run it. Changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` means that anyone who re-runs it (rebuilt schema_migrations, re-run of the migration during a repair/rollback, or a fresh checkout on an existing database) will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and lose its contents instead of failing loudly. Edits to released migrations should not introduce destructive `force: true`; put schema changes in a new migration.

findings.title: New `embed` CSS/JS assets are not added to the precompile list
findings.body: The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is a standalone file, but neither is required from an existing manifest (application.js / application.css) nor added to `config.assets.precompile` in config/application.rb. With `config.assets.compile = false` in production this raises `Sprockets::Rails::Helper::AssetNotPrecompiled` (or serves a 404 for embed.js), so the embed page is unusable in production even though it works in development.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and SSRF
findings.body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes a shell command when the argument starts with `|` (e.g. `|curl evil.com`) and will happily fetch internal addresses (127.0.0.1, link-local metadata endpoints). The setting is admin-controlled, which limits exposure, but it is a needless escalation from "change a site setting" to "run code as the sidekiq user". Use `URI.parse(...).open` / an HTTP client and validate the scheme/host.

findings.title: Loading placeholder is cached for longer than its own reload interval
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to both branches, including the `loading` template, whose inline script reloads the page after 30 seconds. The reload will usually be served from cache, showing the placeholder again without re-checking for the imported topic, so the user waits at least twice as long as intended. Skip the cache headers (or use a much shorter TTL) on the loading response.
